title: Umar's Concern for the People
paragraphs: As a leader, Umar ibn al-Khattab was known for personally checking on the wellbeing of ordinary people at night, sometimes discovering hardships that nobody had formally reported to him.
On one occasion, he found a family struggling with hunger and immediately carried supplies to them himself rather than simply sending someone else to handle the matter on his behalf.
Those around him were surprised that a leader with such responsibility would personally involve himself in such a small, individual case instead of delegating it entirely to an assistant.

Leaders today sometimes reference this story when discussing genuine accountability. It shows that real leadership sometimes means noticing individual struggles personally, not only managing situations from a distance.
